# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 33 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 33 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_033_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 5, Chapter 1 — Patience and Anger

**1** "Be patient and long-suffering," he said. "If you develop patience, it will give you mastery over every kind of wickedness and you'll be able to practice all righteousness. **2** Here's how it works: when you are patient, the Holy Spirit who lives inside you stays pure — untainted by any other spirit. He has room to breathe; he lives in a spacious, open place, full of joy. And together with you — the vessel he lives in — he serves the Lord with great gladness and inner peace. **3** But when anger moves in, everything changes. The Holy Spirit is delicate, and he feels cramped immediately. There's no clean place left for him; he starts looking for a way out. The angry spirit chokes him out — crowds him and pollutes him so he can't serve the Lord the way he wants to. The reason is this: the Lord lives in patience, but the devil lives in anger. **4** When both spirits try to share the same space — the moment the angry one enters — the Holy Spirit is grieved and leaves that person. **5** The patient spirit is precious to God and welcome before him; the Lord makes his home in patience. The angry spirit, on the other hand, is worth nothing, and it destroys whoever it inhabits."

---

*PNEUMA note: The image of the Holy Spirit as "delicate" and needing "room to breathe" is one of the most tender descriptions of the Spirit in any early Christian text. It is pastoral rather than systematic — about spiritual climate, not just spiritual categories.*
